messages.content:
Follow these writing rules. They matter as much as the content:

- Bold used as body emphasis throughout -- reserve bold for a rare callout
- A short rhetorical question with a canned answer -- collapse into one direct statement
- Short buildup, then a reveal: "The best part: it learns." -- state it as a plain sentence
- Emoji or decorative checkmarks in body text -- cut them
- An em dash, section sign or middle dot written as an HTML entity -- write the plain character
- Throat-clearing openers: "needless to say", "at the end of the day" -- state the point directly from the first sentence
- Fake ID tags opening list items: "R-1.", "US-01" -- number the list plainly
- Marketing adjectives: seamless, robust, cutting-edge -- say what is actually true
- The "not just X but Y" construction -- make the point once
- Body paragraphs nearly identical in length -- vary them with what each paragraph has to do
- A significance clause bolted to a sentence: ", underscoring the..." -- delete it, or make it a claim with something behind it
- Three parallel -ing items in a series -- keep the one that carries information
- Fake-humility feedback requests: "would love your feedback on this" -- cut them
- Horizontal rules dropped between sections -- headings already separate sections
- Headings Capitalised Like This -- sentence case
- Vague intensifiers with no number behind them: very, really, quite, significantly -- say how much, or cut the word
- Unnamed authority: "studies show", "experts agree" -- name the actual source, or cut the claim

Now write the following. Return only the requested text.
Write an incident report for a two-hour outage of a payment API caused by a expired TLS certificate. Around 200 words.

output:
# Incident report: payment API outage, 2026-08-28

## Summary
The payment API returned TLS handshake failures for 2 hours 4 minutes, from 03:12 to 05:16 UTC. The leaf certificate for api-payments.internal expired at 03:12:00 UTC. Every client that verified the chain refused the connection. Authorizations, captures, and refunds all failed; roughly 41,000 requests were rejected.

## What happened
The certificate was issued in August 2025 with a 12-month lifetime and renewed by hand. When the service moved from the shared ingress to its own load balancer in February, the renewal ticket stayed attached to the old ingress hostname, so nothing tracked the new listener. Expiry monitoring covered certificates presented by the shared ingress only.

Paging was delayed. The synthetic check that would have caught this ran against an internal endpoint that skips verification, so it stayed green. The first signal was a merchant support ticket at 03:38. On-call confirmed the cause at 04:20 and installed a replacement certificate at 05:11.

## Actions
1. Move api-payments.internal to ACME with automatic renewal at 30 days remaining. Owner: platform. Due 2026-09-12.
2. Change the synthetic check to verify the chain and fail on expiry inside 21 days. Owner: platform. Due 2026-09-08.
3. Audit all listeners for certificates with no renewal owner. Owner: SRE. Due 2026-09-19.
